title: Engineers India Ltd - 532178 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: placeholder
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 turnover was INR802 crore, flat QoQ against INR800 crore, while PBT rose about 58% to INR229 crore and PAT about 65% to INR180 crore. Operating margin expanded to 19% from 14% in Q1, helped by a consultancy segment margin of about 30%, which management said had no one-time items. The mix shifted to 68% consultancy and 32% turnkey in H1 from 47:53 a year earlier. Order book reached a record INR20,421 crore, and management said order inflow had reached about INR8,100 crore to date against the INR8,000 crore target.

segments.name: Consultancy & Engineering
segments.commentary: Q2 turnover INR594 crore; H1 turnover INR1,093 crore (68% of H1 mix vs 47% a year earlier). Q2 segment margin about 30%, management said no one-time items; H1 segment margin about 27.7-28%.

segments.commentary: Q2 turnover INR208 crore; H1 turnover INR510 crore (32% of H1 mix vs 53%). Management cited new-project cost ramp-up keeping margins around 4-5%, versus 6-7% historically; depository-type orders carry about 7% margin as plant and material cost sits in revenue.

segments.name: Ramagundam (RFC)
segments.commentary: Profit of INR20 crore in Q2 and INR42 crore in Q1, INR63 crore for H1 FY27 per management.

qa_highlights.question: Was there a one-off in the consultancy segment given the roughly 30% margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed about 30% in Q2 with no one-time item; the mix shift to consultancy (68%) explains higher margin, and a 24-25% full-year margin is expected.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company revise its INR8,000 crore order inflow target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will cross INR8,000 crore and expects to revise guidance next time, with INR8,100 crore secured to date.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue and margin guidance applies to FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated about INR4,200-4,300 crore FY27 revenue and about 10% growth for FY28, with EBITDA margin protected by the higher consultancy mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for nuclear and Middle East orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Nuclear opportunities are at study or EIA stage and orders are expected in about a year; Middle East orders are on hold pending stabilisation, with Saudi still uncertain.

qa_highlights.question: Are change orders and provision write-backs expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said many change orders are being negotiated and are expected to be settled within FY27; no quantification was given.

qa_highlights.question: What drove other income of INR65 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Dividends of INR21 crore from NRL and INR11 crore from CEIL, with the rest from regular income, surplus fund income and rent; dividends expected on an ongoing basis.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue of around INR4,200-4,300 crore; management said FY28 growth of around 10% on the current order book, with a possible upgrade later.
Consultancy share of FY27 revenue expected at around 60% (management cited 60-65% range), with turnkey execution expected to reach at least 40% in H2.
Consultancy segment margin to be maintained at about 24-25% on a full-year basis; management said Q2 and H1 margins would be higher than 25%, but did not commit to 30%.
EBITDA margin expected to be maintained, per management, as consultancy mix rises (earlier guidance cited 15-16%).
Order inflow target of INR8,000 crore for FY27; management said it expects to cross this, with INR8,100 crore secured to date. FY28 inflow expected at least INR8,000-8,100 crore.
Change orders under negotiation with clients expected to be settled within FY27.
Nuclear opportunities expected to convert to orders in about a year, with next financial year seen as the earliest meaningful win period.
capex_capacity: Order book at INR20,421 crore as on 30 September 2026, up from INR14,424 crore on 30 June 2026 (all-time high); about 75% consultancy and about 55-60% overseas.
Order book projects to be delivered over three to four years; Dangote project execution cited as four to five years.
Company implementing a CBG plant with its own investment and considering a second CBG plant.
Strategic crude storage tenders from ISPRL (including Bina, MP, and two-three other locations) identified as opportunities; coal gasification studies under way with bids for major projects.
demand_pricing: Order inflow H1 FY27 at INR7,428 crore: INR5,762 crore consultancy and INR1,666 crore turnkey.
Order inflow to date stated at INR8,100 crore (about INR670 crore added after the H1 figure); Middle East share about INR500-600 crore.
Middle East (Saudi) orders stalled due to ongoing conflict; Africa recovered as a source of business; management expects Middle East tenders to revive only after stabilisation.
Dangote project (Africa, awarded around January 2026) in engineering phase; management did not give percentage completion.

Domestic pipeline cited: AP refinery (BPCL Andhra), IOCL Paradip Phase 2 (awaiting client land), BPCL revamps, strategic storage, nonferrous smelter projects, fertilizer, a data centre project and nuclear balance-of-plant and environmental studies.
Competition: management did not give win-rate figures; said it has beaten competitors on mega jobs.
Payment terms on overseas consultancy are progress-linked; management said it does not work with unknown clients.
risks_watch: Middle East conflict continuing, with Saudi orders (including the expected Aramco agreement) stalled; management gave no timeline beyond the next one to two quarters.
Consultancy margin of about 30% in Q2 may not repeat; management guided 24-25% for the full year.
Turnkey margins at about 4-5% on new projects, below the historical 6-7% range, and turnkey share of revenue below earlier expectations.
Dangote project in Kenya faces an ongoing court case; management said the owner handles legal matters and engineering work continues.
CPSE pay revision timing unknown; management said it cannot predict when it will come, with a labour cost impact to follow.
Order inflow relies on a few large awards; management said project timing is hard to predict.
key_quotes: Company's order book position has reached its all-time high and stands at INR20,421 crores as on 30th September 2026 as compared to INR14,424 crores as on 30th June 2026.
Definitely, we will maintain our 24%, 25% segment profit in the consultancy segment on overall basis, yearly basis.
And as such, there is no onetime item.
As of today, we stand at INR8,100 crores.
summary.management_tone: Confident on near-term numbers and the order book, but cautious and non-committal on the Middle East, nuclear timing, and specific margin or order targets beyond the current year. Several answers were vague or deferred to the other speaker.

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided at around INR4,200-4,300 crore (midpoint 4,250 vs FY26 flat-to-down implied by H1 INR1,603 crore vs INR1,758 crore), backed by a record INR20,421 crore order book and INR8,100 crore inflow to date; no new capacity, delivery shown as order execution over 3-4 years.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin is guided to be maintained as the consultancy mix rises to about 60% of FY27 revenue, but H1 EBITDA was 23% against 15-16% guidance and the full-year consultancy margin is guided at 24-25%, so further expansion is not committed.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plant or capacity was guided; order book of INR20,421 crore is to be executed over 3-4 years, with a CBG plant and a second CBG plant only under consideration.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Record INR20,421 crore order book and INR8,100 crore inflow to date support FY27 revenue of INR4,200-4,300 crore, but H1 turnover fell to INR1,603 crore from INR1,758 crore (about -9%).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management is implementing a CBG plant with its own investment and considering a second one, plus ISPRL storage tenders and coal gasification bids, but no capex figure or date was given.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management said it will cross the INR8,000 crore order inflow target (INR8,100 crore secured to date) and expects to revise guidance next time, with FY28 growth around 10% and a possible upgrade later.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q2 consultancy margin of about 30% may not repeat against FY guidance of 24-25%, Middle East orders are stalled, and turnkey margins are 4-5% versus 6-7% historically.

rows.label: Nuclear orders expected to convert
rows.why: Nuclear opportunities are at study or EIA stage, with management seeing the next financial year as the earliest meaningful win period.

rows.label: Change order settlements within FY27
rows.why: Many change orders are under negotiation and expected to be settled within FY27, though no amount was quantified.

rows.label: Middle East orders revival
rows.why: Saudi orders are stalled by the conflict, with about INR500-600 crore of Middle East share in inflow to date and no timeline beyond one to two quarters.

tone.note: Management was confident on the record order book, the INR8,100 crore inflow to date and FY27 revenue of INR4,200-4,300 crore, but cautious on the Middle East, nuclear timing and margins beyond the current year. Analysts pushed on the one-off nature of the Q2 consultancy margin of about 30%.
